we design an algorithm for the optimal management of a 5G network infrastructure, which maximises the provider’s revenue while ensuring that the service guarantees are met, and we prove that it performs close to the theoretical optimum.

we design and implement an adaptive algorithm that maximises the infrastructure providers’ revenue while ensuring the service guarantees provided by the infrastructure provider to tenants are satisfied.
we propose a new algorithm that optimises the infrastructure provider’s revenue while ensuring that the service level agreements provided to the tenants are satisfied.

the optimisation of 5G infrastructure provider's revenue in a network slicing-enabled 5G network.
a fundamental question: how to optimise the business of network slicing in 5G networks?

a key challenge for 5G: how to design efficient algorithms for the management of 5G infrastructure resources in a network slicing-capapable environment, where new players (the infrastructure provider and the tenants) are introduced in the ecosystem.

the proposed solution is a novel, effective, and efficient approach to network slicing that can be applied to 5G networks.

we have developed an algorithm for the optimal allocation of network slices that is able to achieve close to optimal performance and can be used by the infrastructure provider for the admission of tenants in a network slicing-capapable 5G network.

our work is a significant contribution in terms of the design of algorithms to optimise the allocation of network slices in 5G networks, which are the basis for the development of new business models in the mobile network ecosystem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a novel adaptive network slicing admission control and allocation algorithm for 5G networks that achieves close to the optimal performance.
we provide a framework to design a revenue maximising algorithm for network slicing that is adaptive and robust.
we provide a new framework for the optimisation of network slicing in 5G networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the network slicing paradigm is expected to bring substantial performance benefits, it also introduces new challenges in terms of the design of efficient algorithms for the admission and management of network slices.
network slicing is not only a technology that allows to improve performance, but it is also a key enabler for the optimisation of 5G infrastructure market.
, by using the right admission control policy, the infrastructure provider can maximise its revenue, even when the tenants are not cooperative.
